name: European Union

sources.title: Directive (EU) 2019/882 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 April 2019 on the accessibility requirements for products and services
sources.note: ELI http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj. EUR-Lex lists the act as in force, with corrigenda for the DE, ET, FI, FR and HR versions only. Proposal 52026PC0590 would amend it; not adopted, not reviewed.

sources.title: European Commission: harmonised standards, list of references published in the OJEU
European Commission: harmonised standards for websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies (Directive (EU) 2016/2102)
sources.note: Cited to show where EN 301 549 IS cited: under the Web Accessibility Directive, not the EAA.

citations.quote: They shall apply those measures from 28 June 2025.

applicationDate.note: Article 31(3) lets member states apply Article 4(8), answering emergency calls to 112, from 28 June 2027 at the latest.

citations.quote: Member States shall adopt and publish, by 28 June 2022, the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply
Microenterprises providing services shall be exempt from complying with the accessibility requirements referred to in paragraph 3 of this Article

microenterpriseExemption.note: Services only. Microenterprises dealing in products get lighter obligations elsewhere, not this exemption.

value.test: fewer than 10 persons employed, and annual turnover or annual balance sheet total of at most EUR 2 million

citations.quote: ‘microenterprise’ means an enterprise which employs fewer than 10 persons … annual balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 2 million
citations.note: Omitted at the ellipsis: 'and which has an annual turnover not exceeding EUR 2 million or an'.

value.basis: harmonised standards whose references are published in the Official Journal

citations.quote: published in the Official Journal of the European Union, shall be presumed to be in conformity with the accessibility requirements

value.summary: Member states set the penalties. They must be effective, proportionate and dissuasive and come with remedial action. The directive sets no amounts.

citations.quote: The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

value.rule: Service contracts agreed before 28 June 2025 may continue unaltered until they expire, but no longer than five years from that date.

citations.quote: Service contracts agreed before 28 June 2025 may continue … but no longer than five years from that date.
citations.note: Omitted at the ellipsis: 'without alteration until they expire,'.

transitionalServiceContracts.note: The text states a five-year period, not a calendar date. Sweden and Germany write the end date as 27 June 2030.

value.rule: Member state option: terminals lawfully used before 28 June 2025 may stay in use to the end of their economically useful life.

citations.quote: until the end of their economically useful life, but no longer than 20 years after their entry into use

citations.pinpoint: References of harmonised standards and of other European standards published in the OJEU, group 'Accessibility'
citations.quote: Websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies
citations.note: The only entry under Accessibility. There is no entry for Directive (EU) 2019/882 or for products and services.
Implementing Decision (EU) 2018/2048, as amended on 11 August 2021. A citation under the Web Accessibility Directive; it does not carry over to the EAA.

harmonisation.note: An exact-phrase EUR-Lex search for "in support of Directive (EU) 2019/882" returned no results on 2026-11-08. A search result page is not a stable source, so it is recorded here rather than cited.

unverified: A Commission Implementing Decision publishing references of harmonised standards in support of Directive (EU) 2019/882: none found on EUR-Lex or on the Commission harmonised-standards pages (2026-11-08).
A fixed calendar end date for the self-service-terminal transition (Article 32(2)): the text sets no such date, only 'no longer than 20 years after their entry into use'.
An explicit end date for service contracts in Article 32(1), second subparagraph: the text says 'five years from that date' (28 June 2025). 2030-06-28 is worked out from that.
The content of pending amendment proposal 52026PC0590 was not reviewed for effects on these claims.
